samples.question: The picture shows one array of 6 rows and 6 columns of equal square cells, enclosed by a blue frame; each cell is filled with a single flat grey and the cell edges are not drawn. One corner cell of the array carries a small orange square: that is the corner reference cell. Turn the picture so that the marked corner cell is at the top left, and use that orientation for everything below. The top row and the left column of the array are blank unprinted paper. The remaining 5 rows and 5 columns form the printed panel. The sheet was lit unevenly, so the brightness of a cell is its printed tone multiplied by the lighting at that cell, and the two blank strips record that lighting: the lighting at a panel cell equals the brightness of the blank cell at the top of its column, times the brightness of the blank cell at the left of its row, divided by the brightness of the marked corner cell. Divide the brightness of each panel cell by that lighting to recover its printed tone. Every panel cell is printed in one of exactly two tones, a dark one at about 0.40 of blank paper and a light one at about 0.77 of blank paper, and exactly 9 of the 25 panel cells carry the dark tone. Those 9 dark-tone cells form a shape that most closely matches one of these six symbols: eff, ex, plus, tee, vee, zee. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.
